$comment: Treasure maps (docs/design/famous-pirates-and-treasure.md, slice 3). A famous pirate's hoard holds 'hoardShare' of his wealth when it is placed, which is when the captain gets the first piece of its map: on a coastal land tile 'placeTiles' from one of his haunts, at least 'clearOfTownsTiles' from any town, by a landmark. The chart rings the search area, 'ringTiles' across by pieces held (1 to 4); the ring's centre lies off the hoard by up to 'ringOffset' of the widest ring, closing on it as the ring shrinks, so the hoard is always inside. A shady stranger sits in a town's tavern some weeks ('stranger.chance', or 'unfinishedChance' while the captain holds an unfinished map) and sells a piece of one pirate's map for 'priceShare' of the hoard's worth (at least 'minPrice'): an unfinished map is 'unfinishedWeight' times likelier, a pirate whose haven or haunts lie within 'nearTiles' 'nearWeight' times. Sinking a famous pirate, a survivor picked from the water carries a piece of his map with 'survivorChance'. Digging (slice 4): the men go ashore on the nearest beach within 'dig.reachTiles' of the ship and dig for 'dig.hours'; within 'dig.toleranceTiles' of a hoard whose map the captain holds a piece of, it comes up (its gold to the plunder chest, out of the pirate's wealth, and 'dig.fame'); otherwise, inside a map's search ring, the men see its landmark and say which way it lies and how far. A hoard dug up before its pirate was ever beaten sets him on revenge: he hunts the captain at any odds, from 'dig.revengeReach' times as far, until he is beaten.
